opportunities.description: Learn the basics of 3D design with Tinkercad - a free web app for everyone. By combining simple shapes, it is possible to create complex designs and potentially, 3D print the result with ease. Registration is required. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: (九月專題：新學期，新起點！新移民家庭的「開學收心指南」) Back-to-School Reset – Building Healthy Routines and Digital Habits
opportunities.description: Join Family Services York Region for a practical Back-to-School Reset! This session is facilitated in Mandarin and is perfect for newcomer families. Gain tools for smoother transitions and balanced tech use. Participants will learn: How to establish healthy family routines. How to manage screen time. How to build positive digital habits that support your child’s success in schools. 開學了，如何幫助孩子收心？ 總是為了手機、電腦和孩子吵架？ 誠邀您參加 「 開學收心指南」實用講座！ 一起解鎖健康家庭作息、合理控管螢幕時間，培養健康的電子產品使用習慣。 *The program's facilitator also speaks Cantonese*
opportunities.address: Milliken Mills Branch, 7600 Kennedy Road, Unit 1, Markham, Ontario, L3R 9S5

opportunities.title: L'univers sombre et magnifique
opportunities.description: Depuis des millénaires, les êtres humains contemplent le ciel nocturne et s'interrogent sur l'origine de l'univers. D'où vient-il ? De quoi est-ce fait? Où va-t-il? Dans cette présentation, Renée Hložek vous parlerai de cet univers — à la fois sombre et magnifique — et de la manière dont nous utilisons les télescopes pour en percer les secrets. Renée Hložek est cosmologiste sud-africaine et professeure agrégée au Dunlap Institute for Astronomy & Astrophysics de l’Université de Toronto. Ses recherches portent sur les origines et l’évolution de l’Univers, notamment le fond diffus cosmologique, l’énergie noire et la matière noire. Elle participe à d’importantes collaborations internationales, telles que l’Atacama Cosmology Telescope, le Simons Observatory et le Vera C. Rubin Observatory. Elle a reçu la médaille du roi Charles III pour la communication d’idées scientifiques, ainsi que la médaille Rutherford et la bourse Arthur B. McDonald du Conseil de recherches en sciences naturelles et en génie du Canada. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8. ACCESSIBILITÉ Le sous-titrage en direct ou automatique, l’interprétation en langue des signes, les services d’intervenant, ou les services d’accompagnement sont disponibles sur demande. Veuillez soumettre votre demande au moins deux semaines à l’avance à : tpl.ca/accessibility-events .

opportunities.title: Homeschoolers Weekly Meet-Up @ Angus Glen
opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! Passive Worksheets (Wordsearches & Colouring) + Kapla Blocks & Challenge Cards + Guest Speaker Day speaker from City of Markham's Environmental Services, 11am-12 noon PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. We ask that all participants (caregivers and children) please sign-up for each session to guarantee your spot! *** ***For example, if there is 1 caregiver and 3 children attending, please indicate 4 in the registration.
opportunities.address: Angus Glen Branch, 3990 Major Mackenzie Drive East, Markham, Ontario, L6C 1P8

opportunities.title: Computers for Beginners 3: Use the Internet
opportunities.description: An introductory class on the Internet for absolute beginners with little computer experience. In this third session you will: Understand how to read a web site address Practice using web addresses Search for information using a search engine Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches. Prerequisites: Computer for Beginners 1 & 2 or basic mouse and keyboarding skills Format: Hands-on with demonstrations Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.description: Are you interested in how to navigate the internet on your personal devices with improved privacy and understanding the importance of staying safe using social media? If so, this is the class for you. In this program, you will: How to use public computing environments with improved privacy Navigate the Internet on your personal devices with improved privacy Reduce privacy risks through the use of web browser plug-ins/extensions Understand the privacy considerations of using social media Pre-Requisites : Some computer experience is required ; the ability to navigate app menus, browsers, and desktop computing features is desirable.

opportunities.description: Computers for Beginners 2: Use the Keyboard A class on basic keyboard functions for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience. Prerequisites: Computer for Beginners 1 or basic mouse skills Format: Hands-on with demonstrations Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Snacks are offered during the After School Club for participants. Ingredient lists will be available. Snacks are generously supported, in part, by donors. After School Club: Dash and Dot Join us as we learn the basics of coding using Dash and Dot robots! Take control as you guide your robot through a series of challenges! No registration required

opportunities.title: Introduction to 3D Printing
opportunities.description: Learn how 3D printers work and how you can print at the Toronto Public Library’s Digital Innovation Hubs. This class includes hands-on instruction with Prusa Slicer, the software used to prepare your 3D object file for printing on a Prusa MK3S+ 3D printer. Note: Customers are no longer required to attend a mandatory 3D printing class prior to using a 3D printer at the Toronto Public Library’s Digital Innovation Hubs. This class is for those who are interested in learning more about 3D printing and how to use the Prusa software. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: Five Pieces of the AI Puzzle
opportunities.description: This interactive 60-minute session demystifies artificial intelligence through a unique five-piece puzzle framework, guiding participants to better understand AI’s presence, challenge common perceptions, and actively shape how they live and work alongside it. Combining multimedia, collaboration, and real-world examples, the program empowers audiences to move beyond passive awareness toward confident, informed engagement with AI. This is a multi-media presentation with video clips, props, group discussion and begins with an opening Puzzle Pieces song and an actual solve a 5-piece puzzle challenge ice breaker. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca, 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8
opportunities.address: Guildwood, 123 Guildwood Parkway, Toronto, ON, M1E 4V2

opportunities.title: Makerspace Tour: Markham Village
opportunities.description: Join us in celebrating Digital Innovation Month by attending our Makerspace Tour Series! Are you curious about the makerspace ? Not sure what you can expect out of them? Whether you want to scan your great-grandparent's slides, make your own coasters with the laser engraver, 3D Print a t-rex or record your first album, there are many ways Markham Public Library can help you inspire you and get you started on your path to being a maker. Now is your chance to visit any of our five unique Makerspaces to meet our dedicated Digital Literacy Specialists, and learn about the tools and services available to you! Note: This is in a drop-in tour - arrive when you can, and stay as long as you want!

opportunities.title: Introduction to Recording Voiceover for Film in Audacity
opportunities.description: Want to learn how to add custom audio to your films and videos? Perhaps a voiceover? Join us in our Introduction to Recording Voiceover for Film in Audacity workshop! Audacity is an easy-to-use, multi-track audio editor and recorder for Windows, macOS, GNU/Linux and other operating systems. Audacity is a Digital Audio Workstation (DAW) that is FREE to download. This makerspace demonstration will provide instruction on how to use this program to get you started with sound editing and recording. We will cover how to edit sound, what effects this program has to offer on your vocals and how to mix down your different tracks. At the end of the session you will receive a quick tour of Markham Village's sound booth and more information on how to book the space. With your new skills, why not participate in our upcoming Markham Village Film Festival ? Hope to see you there. Become Maker Certified Please note: if you are looking to use our makerspaces independently, you must be 13+ and complete this online Makerspace module . Once completed, our staff can update your profile and you will be maker certified!

opportunities.title: Makerspace Tour: Thornhill Community Centre
opportunities.description: Join us in celebrating Digital Innovation Month by attending our Makerspace Tour Series! Are you curious about the makerspace ? Not sure what you can expect out of them? Whether you want to scan your great-grandparent's slides, make your own coasters with the laser engraver, 3D Print a t-rex or record your first album, there are many ways Markham Public Library can help you inspire you and get you started on your path to being a maker. Now is your chance to visit any of our five unique Makerspaces to meet our dedicated Digital Literacy Specialists, and learn about the tools and services available to you! Note: This is in a drop-in tour - arrive when you can, and stay as long as you want!

opportunities.title: Homeschoolers Weekly Meet-Up @ Angus Glen
opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. We ask that all participants (caregivers and children) please sign-up for each session to guarantee your spot! *** ***For example, if there is 1 caregiver and 3 children attending, please indicate 4 in the registration.

opportunities.description: Are you interested in starting a career in the field of health care? Or perhaps you work in the health care field and are looking to add to your education to move into a new area of health care? We’ll highlight important things such as: We will cover programs such as Personal Support Worker, Practical Nursing, Registered Nursing and Medical Device Reprocessing We will cover programs in the field of Science We will touch on entrance requirements, steps to apply A bit about financial aid and student supports **Please note: This workshop is run in partnership with Seneca Polytechnic**. _______ Registrants will receive an email with the Zoom link 1 day prior to the program. If you do not receive the Zoom link the day before the program: Check your email inbox and spam folders. If you still cannot find the email, please contact us at mplcommunitylibrarians@markhamlibrary.ca prior to the program start time so we can provide you with the link.

opportunities.title: Be An Active Digital Citizen - Play-based Workshop for Families
opportunities.description: In this play-based, interactive workshop for children and families, we explore what it means to be a smart, safe, and empowered digital citizen. Through games and hands-on activities, children will practice healthy social media habits and learn about their digital rights online in a fun, age-appropriate way. At the end of this workshop, participants should: Be able to recognize healthy vs. unhealthy social media habits and practice simple strategies for balanced use. Understand basic digital rights for children online (i.e. privacy, safety, expression). Build confidence identifying safe, respectful ways to engage with others online, both individually and as a family. Note: this session is intended to be intended by families including children aged 8 - 16 and their parents/caregivers . Please register for each individual attending. Hosted by Kids Rights Canada .

opportunities.title: CyberSafe Seniors, Preventing AI Fraud and Scams
opportunities.description: CyberSafe Seniors, Preventing AI Fraud and Scams which addresses the growing threat of AI-enabled online fraud and scams targeting older Canadians. As AI tools become more accessible, scammers are using tactics such as voice cloning, deepfake videos, and highly convincing phishing techniques to impersonate loved ones and fabricate financial emergencies. Older adults aged 55+ are disproportionately targeted, often experiencing significant financial loss along with shame, anxiety, and social isolation. Through workshops delivered by MediaSmarts experts participants will learn how AI-enabled scams work, how to verify messages from family or financial institutions, and what steps to take if targeted.

opportunities.title: How We Stay Relevant in the Age of AI
opportunities.description: AI is changing how people think about work, learning, and human value. Many professionals, parents, students, and community members are asking a very real question: if AI can generate answers, summaries, explanations, drafts, code, and ideas so quickly, where do humans remain relevant? This session argues that humans should not try to compete with AI at speed, recall, or routine output. That is the wrong competition. As AI makes answers easier to produce, human value moves toward deeper understanding, disciplined curiosity, judgment, and the ability to question, verify, and ground what AI produces. For most of us, learning has often been treated as natural and implicit. We were taught subjects in school, but not always taught how learning itself works. Machine learning gives us a useful mirror. In order to teach machines how to learn, humans had to make parts of learning explicit: objectives, data, patterns, prediction, feedback, error correction, validation, calibration, and updating. This session uses those machine learning principles not as a technical lesson, but as a way to think about how humans can learn more deeply in the age of AI. Participants will explore why superficial knowledge is becoming less survivable, why AI still needs to be grounded in human reality, and how disciplined curiosity can help people remain valuable as AI becomes more capable. The session will include a short lecture-style presentation followed by a guided audience discussion. The discussion can be shaped around a small number of reflection questions, with flexibility to shift into Q&A or a brief example/demo depending on the audience engagement and MPL’s preference. No technical background is required. By the end of this session, participants will be able to: Explain why shallow learning and routine knowledge work become more vulnerable when AI can generate fluent answers quickly. Apply key machine learning principles, such as objective-setting, feedback, error correction, validation, calibration, and updating, as a practical framework for deeper human learning, better questioning, and stronger judgment. Bio: Darren Soo is a Canadian technology founder and creator of PI, an individualized AI reasoning framework designed to help people reason through complex, changing information over time. His background spans more than two decades of practical technology work across enterprise and operational software environments. His current work centres on artificial intelligence, machine learning, and explainable reasoning systems, while his broader interests include how technology can support curiosity, better questions, learning and decision-making.

Learning Outcomes Apply practical fact-checking strategies to evaluate the accuracy and credibility of information related to elections and current events. opportunities.title: Makerspace Tour: Aaniin
opportunities.description: Join us in celebrating Digital Innovation Month by attending our Makerspace Tour Series! Are you curious about the makerspace ? Not sure what you can expect out of them? Whether you want to scan your great-grandparent's slides, make your own coasters with the laser engraver, 3D Print a t-rex or record your first album, there are many ways Markham Public Library can help you inspire you and get you started on your path to being a maker. Now is your chance to visit any of our five unique Makerspaces to meet our dedicated Digital Literacy Specialists, and learn about the tools and services available to you! Note: This is in a drop-in tour - arrive when you can, and stay as long as you want!
opportunities.address: Aaniin Branch, 5665 14th Avenue, Markham, Ontario, L3S 3K5

opportunities.title: Homeschoolers Weekly Meet-Up @ Angus Glen
opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. We ask that all participants (caregivers and children) please sign-up for each session to guarantee your spot! *** ***For example, if there is 1 caregiver and 3 children attending, please indicate 4 in the registration.
opportunities.address: Angus Glen Branch, 3990 Major Mackenzie Drive East, Markham, Ontario, L6C 1P8

opportunities.title: AI Powered Job Search
opportunities.description: Are you using AI in your job search journey? Learn how to use AI to make your job search easier and more effective. In this workshop, you'll discover how AI can help you improve your resume, tailor it for Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS), find jobs that match your skills, prepare for interviews, research employers, and stay organized throughout your job search. You'll also learn how to use AI safely and responsibly, with practical tips and prompts you can start using right away. No experience with AI is required. Learning outcomes: - discover how AI can help you improve your resume - discover how AI can help you with your whole job searching journey - learn how to use AI safely and responsibly in your job searching journey Presenter's bio: This workshop is facilitated by VPI Employment Services. Since 1988, VPI Employment Services have been delivering employment services to help individuals, employers, and communities achieve their goals at no cost . Their work focuses on providing tailored employment programs, vocational assessments, and supportive services to jobseekers that help build job readiness, provide access to training, and connect them with meaningful and sustainable employment opportunities.

opportunities.title: Creative Writing in the AI Apocalypse: Community Conversation with Joseph Donato
opportunities.description: How will writers survive the age of Artificial Intelligence?” Everyone’s got a story to tell, but the threat generative AI poses on the creative arts may discourage writers from putting pen to paper. Join this Community Conversation to understand the role of writers today, share your opinions on creative writing in an AI world, and engage with some related writing prompts. Joseph Donato is a Queer writer, editor, and library worker. He has completed his MFA in Creative Writing at the University of Guelph, and his most recent poetry chapbook, No One Should Be Happy When I'm Not was published in 2026. Joseph's poems have appeared in The Ampersand Review, Pinhole Magazine, and more. He enjoys dad rock, money, and being afraid. He can be found @josephdonato13 on Instagram or josephdonato.ca .

opportunities.title: Tips and Tricks to Master the IB Physics and IB Math Internal Assessment
opportunities.description: Join us for a 60-minute workshop designed to help IB students excel in their Internal Assessment (IA) for Math and Physics! Led by experienced IB educator and author of “7 Steps to a 7”, this session will provide valuable insights into the expectations and criteria for a successful IA. Learn how to choose a strong research question, avoid common pitfalls, manage your time effectively, and maximize your marks with expert tips and strategies. Whether you're just starting your IA or looking for guidance on revisions, this program will give you the tools you need to succeed in your IB coursework . Don’t miss out—sign up today! ** Please note: This program is run in partnership with Julia, a certified high school teacher of IB Physics SL and IB Math SL and creator of Physics in the Flesh (YouTube Channel) _____________________ Registrants will receive an email with the Zoom link 1 day prior to the program. If you do not receive the Zoom link the day before the program: Check your email inbox and spam folders. If you still cannot find the email, please contact us at mplcommunitylibrarians@markhamlibrary.ca prior to the program start time so we can provide you with the link.

YPAM in partnership with the Markham Public Library provides this weekly literacy program, where volunteers read grade specific books for children in Junior Kindergarten, Senior Kindergarten, Grade 1, Grade 2 and IEP kids. Make Reading to Success part of your child's reading habit and build a love of reading together. To register, please visit: https://www.ypam.ca/reading *Please note that through registering, you are giving YPAM your information.
